title: Prove the complete fixed P104 R22 compiler tail envelope
body:
The PR5756 invoice has a favorable moment, but compiler tails also restrict its parameters. This package proves that `(cutoff,floor)=(16,17)` is the only integer pair for its existing 128-block tail contract. It covers every positive offset and every permitted rational decay. The full offset interval has endpoints near `.0901726680035` and `.193311515488`; the unique optimum is near `.141270802755`, with decay infimum `.975481788192714…`. The old offset `1/5` fails for every permitted decay.

Source [PR5756](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5756) is pinned at `a1b338e5d9271b541f2a198f4fc19cefc565feed`. Its complete JSON invoice has 66,852 paid calls and 13,390 targets. The proof uses convexity, monotonicity and directed rational arithmetic. A passing alternate decay shows why a fixed-decay failure alone does not prove infeasibility.

Validation: registered CPython3.12.14 replay; 640 exact rational-power cases; 80 independent Decimal power and 80 log checks; source and alternate passing points; infeasible cutoffs, floors and offsets; missing-count and source-corruption controls. The official scientific export passed `-I -O -B` with empty PATH, no Git and read-only files; all13 files retained bytes and modes. Only validation documentation follows scientific commit `a5cc123d86a17e47eba7a58e2cd6b50ccc536162`. Full-history provenance was unavailable in this shallow checkout; retained and remote source blobs match. Hosted CI and independent human review are pending.

This is a fixed-invoice tail theorem, not native admission, an entire compiler proof, a new kappa or a bound on changed invoices. The selected frontier and five assumptions are unchanged. The active R22 subspace optimization has a distinct scope.

[Canonical claim and handoff](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/5773). Credit Joel Pulikkan/GamingPuzzled PR5756, Ali Romman PR5751, flyingviper PR5718, the retained P104/native/controller contributors, and Jacob Alan Sussman, zxv and Cao Yifan for the compiler gates. New proof and checker by Ali Romman with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance, no subagents; not independent human acceptance. Apache-2.0.
